note: Two production-safety emission facts the skills lean on: the injected Idempotency-Key header that no caller can reach, and the set of models carrying a raw card number. Both decide guidance where being wrong is expensive - a write that looks deduplicated and is not, and a log line that discloses a PAN - so both are asserted rather than trusted.

assertions.claim: Every non-GET operation carries an `Idempotency-Key` header and no GET does; where no parameter feeds it, the value is a generator-injected `Guid.NewGuid()` the caller cannot set.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience - Make the write idempotent at the provider, the injected-header warning

assertions.claim: The models carrying a raw card `number` are exactly the seven the card-data section names, and no response model is among them - responses carry `last_digits` only.
assertions.defends: paypal-getting-started - Card data: LogRequestBody writes PANs to your logs
